predecessors.name: Han dynasty
predecessors.text: Ji Province, 'present day southern Hebei' (Yuan Shao page), governed from Ye

predecessors.name: Gongsun Zan
predecessors.text: You Province, 'covering present-day northern Hebei, Beijing, Tianjin and Liaoning' (End of the Han page, as quoted in the gongsun-zan dossier); Liaodong was Gongsun Du's, so Liaoning is left out

successors.name: Cao Cao
successors.text: the Yuan lands: Ji (Ye, 204), Bing (204), Qing (205), then You

ledger.x: 193: the war with Gongsun Zan over the Qing and Ji frontier.
199: the frontier war ends with the fall of Yijing, 3rd month of Jian'an 4 (14 April to 12 May 199).
200: Guandu. 'In 200, he launched a campaign against his rival Cao Cao but was defeated at the Battle of Guandu.' The page gives no month.
200: Yuan Shao is beaten at Guandu and withdraws north of the river; no Yuan land changes hands.

wars.name: Yuan Shao-Gongsun Zan war
wars.outcome: Yuan Shao drove Tian Kai out of Qing in 193, beat Gongsun Zan at Yijing in 199 and annexed You Province.

wars.name: Battle of Guandu
wars.outcome: Yuan Shao is defeated by Cao Cao; his lands are not yet touched.

wars.name: Cao Cao's conquest of the Yuan lands
wars.outcome: Ye 204, Bing 204, Nanpi and Qing 205, the heirs gone by 207.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; provinces are approximated by modern provinces (Hebei, Shandong, Shanxi, Beijing-Tianjin), the river lines are not surveyed.
